strategies.name: Entity Alignment across Project Graphs
strategies.description: Identify and link equivalent entities across different project knowledge graphs using structural similarities, semantic relationships, and shared attributes
strategies.implementation: Use GNN-based entity alignment to find correspondences between nodes in different project graphs. Calculate alignment confidence scores and propagate them through the network.

strategies.name: Ontology Alignment Ensemble
strategies.description: Apply voting-based fusion across multiple heterogeneous ontology alignment techniques (lexical, structural, semantic)
strategies.implementation: For each cross-project concept pair, compute similarity from multiple dimensions. Combine via weighted voting to produce final alignment.

strategies.name: Virtual Knowledge Graph Integration
strategies.description: Create a unified virtual knowledge graph over multiple project data sources using schema mappings
strategies.implementation: Define mappings between project schemas and a unified ontology. Answer cross-project queries through the virtual layer without moving data.

strategies.name: Cross-Project Concept Coupling via ABSURDIST
strategies.description: Use internal similarity, external similarity, and mutual inhibition to align concepts across project conceptual systems
strategies.implementation: Model each project's concepts as nodes in a semantic network. Apply ABSURDIST equations to find optimal cross-project correspondences.

strategies.name: Knowledge Graph Embedding Fusion
strategies.description: Embed all project knowledge graphs into a shared latent space where aligned entities cluster together
strategies.implementation: Train translation-based or semantic matching embeddings on combined multi-project graph. Use alignment seeds to anchor cross-project correspondences.

strategies.name: Integrated Information Maximization (IIT-based)
strategies.description: Use IIT 4.0 formalism to measure and maximize integrated information (Phi) across the OMNI-HUB system
strategies.implementation: Represent OMNI-HUB as a TPM (transition probability matrix). Compute phi_s = min(phi_c, phi_e) over the minimum information partition. Maximize by strengthening irreducible connections.

strategies.name: Phi-Structure Enhancement
strategies.description: Increase both distinctions (phi_d) and relations (phi_r) in the cause-effect structure
strategies.implementation: Phi = sum(phi_d) + sum(phi_r). Add mechanisms that specify maximally irreducible cause-effect states. Ensure overlaps among cause/effect states to create relations.

strategies.name: Perturbational Complexity Index (PCI) Optimization
strategies.description: Apply TMS-EEG-like perturbation-complexity measurement to OMNI-HUB architecture
strategies.implementation: Perturb system components and measure complexity of global response. Higher PCI indicates greater integration. Optimize architecture to maximize PCI.

strategies.name: Information Geometry Decomposition
strategies.description: Use information geometry to decompose total information into integrated vs non-integrated components
strategies.implementation: Compute Phi^G using divergence from product manifold. Identify and eliminate non-integrated information channels. Redirect to integrated pathways.

strategies.name: Global Workspace + IIT Hybrid
strategies.description: Combine Global Neuronal Workspace Theory (GNWT) broadcast with IIT integration
strategies.implementation: Create a global workspace for broadcasting information across projects (GNWT), then measure integration of this broadcast via IIT metrics.

Add redundant but differentiated pathways between project modules to increase both distinctions and relations.

combined_optimization: CPI and H are coupled: better entity alignment (CPI) enables more integrated information flow (H).
Use IIT metrics as the objective function for alignment quality: maximize Phi while maintaining alignment precision.

Target threshold analysis: Phi > 0.55 requires ~55% of system information to be irreducibly integrated.
Consider hierarchical integration: integrate within projects first (local Phi), then across projects (global Phi).

unified_field_notes.status: No direct academic sources found for '64-dimensional unified field theory' or 'phi-pi-e-alpha unification' as specific named theories.
unified_field_notes.analysis: These appear to be OMNI-HUB-specific conceptual frameworks rather than established scientific theories. However, relevant mathematical and physical concepts exist:
related_concepts: IIT proposes that consciousness (quality and quantity) is identical to cause-effect structure (Phi-structure) of a physical substrate
Information geometry provides a unified mathematical framework for measuring information integration
String theory and M-theory involve higher-dimensional unified field descriptions (10, 11, 26 dimensions)
Mathematical constants (phi, pi, e, alpha) appear in various unification attempts but no established unified theory links all four
unified_field_notes.recommendation: Treat OMNI-HUB's 64-dimensional framework as an emergent property of the integrated system rather than a pre-existing physical theory. Use IIT's formalism to derive the effective dimensionality from the system's cause-effect structure.
